column11: Peters et al., J Clin Oncol 2026 (doi:10.1200/JCO-25-02016): median progression-free survival of 3.6 months across 117 patients with previously treated advanced NSCLC given sigvotatug vedotin, a vedotin ADC from the same Seagen platform, in the line PADL1NK-005 enrols. At a constant hazard 0.5^(12/3.6) = 9.9% remain after a year, so 90.1% stop
column12: a platform analogue: PF-08046054's own phase 1 reported a confirmed response rate of 26.7% in 30 NSCLC patients and a median duration of response of 7.8 months, but no progression-free median (abstract 8611). Sigvotatug vedotin's non-squamous taxane-naive subgroup ran 6.4 months (72.7% stopping); PADL1NK-005 takes both histologies and excludes only prior docetaxel, so the whole-population figure is the match. At this turnover revenue is close to the year's new starts times the price

column12: PADL1NK-005 enrols PD-L1 of 1% or more after platinum and a PD-(L)1 antibody, and admits actionable alterations after targeted therapy. Abernethy's second-line share comes from 2012 to 2015 with follow-up to July 2015, before immunotherapy, so it is truncated and leans low; driver-positive patients who reach this line after a TKI are carried at the same rates, and the PD-L1 share is read at diagnosis rather than at second line. column12: a quarter of the untreated pool a year, the rate the sacituzumab tirumotecan and telisotuzumab adizutecan seeds give an ADC displacing chemotherapy in a later line. What it displaces is docetaxel, and no ADC has beaten docetaxel on overall survival in unselected previously treated NSCLC: Trodelvy's EVOKE-01 missed (hazard ratio 0.84, Paz-Ares et al., J Clin Oncol 2024, doi:10.1200/JCO.24.00733) and so did sigvotatug vedotin's SigVie-002, so a positive PADL1NK-005 would take a line with no better regimen in it. It reads out first among the biomarker-selected ADC trials against docetaxel still running, ahead of Emrelis in c-Met overexpressing disease (NCT04928846, December 2028) and Datroway in TROP2-positive non-squamous disease (NCT07291037, January 2029, trials table). The identity carries every eligible patient onto therapy in time: about $3.4bn in the US at the 2036 peak (of $8.7bn in total), against $877mm of US sales in FY2025 for Trodelvy, the later-line ADC nearest in price (asset_revenue_regions), so read the peak as a ceiling

column11: derived: Pfizer generated $23,703mm of free cash flow on $185,759mm of revenue over 2023, 2024 and 2025, a 12.76% margin, against the 33.8% its cost of sales, SG&A and R&D leave. The 2021 and 2022 COVID years are excluded because a 36% margin on a vaccine windfall is not what this company earns. Restated before interest: PFE paid $8,181mm of interest inside operating cash flow over 2023 to 2025, 4.40% of revenue. The free cash flow above is struck after it and the valuation already charges the debt by subtracting net debt, so the charge falls by that much, from 22.18% to 17.77%. Checked at replacement capex: no plant depreciation on file for every year, and no amortisation line to take it out of the combined figure, so the charge stands. Restated without one-off cash: PFE's free cash flow over 2023 to 2025 carried $1,350mm of deal payments in operating cash flow, capital allocation whose assets the book values separately; $63mm of legal settlements; $4,400mm of US transition tax (2023 instalment 1,000mm; 2024 instalment 1,300mm; 2025 instalment 2,100mm). None recurs, so the charge falls from 17.77% to 14.52%. Restated without working capital build: over 2023 to 2025 PFE's cash flow statement shows receivables up $25mm, inventories up $1,462mm, payables down $1,792mm, a working capital build of $3,279mm, 1.77% of revenue. Growth ties that cash up once, not on every product for ever, so the charge falls from 14.52% to 12.66%.
